children: Nuvve Holding Corp. (“Nuvve” or the “Company”) (OTCQB Market: NVVE), a global leader in intelligent energy management and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, today launched an AI-powered forecasting platform that helps battery operators and utilities better anticipate energy market conditions, optimize the use of stationary battery assets and strengthen grid resiliency. The platform is in production use across Nuvve’s own battery portfolio and with initial customers in Europe.

Nuvve’s proprietary AI technology analyzes and synthesizes a broad range of data, including energy market conditions, weather, grid activity, outages, telemetry, policy developments and other factors that influence energy supply, demand and pricing, to generate forecasts and actionable insights. The technology forecasts energy prices and identifies the most valuable opportunities to charge and discharge a battery over the coming days.

“Batteries are extraordinarily valuable assets, but their value depends on how intelligently they are deployed,” said Gregory Poilasne, CEO of Nuvve. “Our AI technology is designed to look beyond a single data point or forecast and bring together the many signals that influence energy markets.”
Nuvve’s AI forecasting platform provides a forward-looking view of those conditions, including:
Energy Price Forecasting
: Forecast energy market prices and identify potential opportunities to optimize battery charging and discharging.
Performance Benchmarking
: Compare actual battery dispatch and revenue performance against the AI’s forecasted optimal strategy to identify opportunities for improvement.
Continuous Intelligence
: Monitor a wide range of market and external signals around the clock rather than relying solely on traditional forecasting models or individual analyst assessments.
Scenario Analysis
: Allow operators to ask “what if” questions and assess how changes in conditions, including temperature, market conditions or other variables, could affect battery performance and potential revenue.
Explainable Insights
: Provide visibility into the factors behind forecasts and recommendations, helping operators understand why the system is reaching a particular conclusion rather than treating AI as a black box.

Nuvve is also applying its AI capabilities to utility load forecasting, where anticipating changes in electricity demand is increasingly important as extreme weather, electrification, distributed energy resources and other factors place new demands on power grids.

The technology helps utilities forecast electricity demand and understand how changing conditions affect supply and demand across their service territories. It also enables scenario planning, allowing utilities to assess potential outcomes, such as how a significant temperature shift could affect future demand or battery dispatch.

“Utilities are facing a much more complex energy environment, where weather, electrification, distributed resources, market volatility and other factors change the balance between supply and demand very quickly,” said Gregory Poilasne. “Our objective is to give utilities an intelligent forecasting layer that continuously evaluates those signals.”
Nuvve expects to extend the platform to its battery activities in Japan and to U.S. wholesale markets, providing a foundation for broader deployment across energy markets.
About Nuvve Holding Corp.

Nuvve powers the future of flexible energy by turning batteries, electric vehicles (EVs), buildings, and distributed assets into dynamic grid resources. At the core is Nuvve’s advanced platform for intelligent energy management and vehicle-to-grid (V2G), orchestrating real-time bidirectional charging, load optimization, and grid services. By harnessing an ecosystem of electrification partners, fleets, stationary storage, and smart EV chargers, Nuvve helps utilities and communities unlock flexibility at scale — enhancing reliability, accelerating electrification, and lowering costs. Nuvve enables a clean energy future where mobility, buildings, and infrastructure work together to support a more resilient, sustainable, and equitable grid.
